defects.justification: http.ListenAndServe uses a zero-config http.Server with no ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout, so slowloris-style clients can exhaust connections.

POST /jobs is unauthenticated, so anyone reaching the API can send arbitrary emails (any recipient, subject, body) through the configured SMTP account -- an open spam/phishing relay -- and trigger file reads/writes under IMAGE_ROOT. README notes no auth, but this is a blocker for anything beyond localhost.

Every submitted job (with payload and result) is stored in q.jobs forever; there is no eviction/TTL, so memory grows without bound under sustained use. QUEUE_SIZE bounds only pending jobs, not retained ones.

image.Decode runs on the source file without checking its dimensions via image.DecodeConfig; maxDimension only bounds the output, so a small image declaring huge dimensions (decompression bomb) can exhaust memory in a worker.

When height is 0 it is derived as sb.Dy()*w/sb.Dx() without re-checking maxDimension; e.g. a 1x10000 source with width 10000 gives h=100,000,000 and image.NewRGBA tries to allocate ~4 TB, panicking/OOMing the process.
smtp.SendMail has no dial/IO timeout and ignores the job context; a slow or blackholed SMTP server blocks a worker forever, and a few such jobs stall the whole pool (Close also hangs on wg.Wait).

The output path '<name>-resized.<ext>' is not confined: os.Create follows an existing symlink at that path (possibly pointing outside IMAGE_ROOT) and silently overwrites any existing file of that name. Would require a fix comment (O_EXCL / re-confine).

Retries use a fixed 2s delay with no exponential backoff or jitter, and every error (including permanent ones like invalid path or SMTP auth failure) is retried. Low impact but worth a fix for transient SMTP outages.
writeJSON discards the json.Encode error, so failed responses go unlogged.
